rubrics.criterion: The shared decoder contract no longer requires every backend to implement capability-reporting members: animation frame timing, playback loop policy, and decode working-set reporting are no longer unconditionally required surface of the shared `Decoder` trait.
rubrics.rationale: This case's central fact is that three capability probes were made required members of the one trait every input backend implements; the resolution stands or falls on their removal from the shared contract.

rubrics.criterion: A reachable capability surface still supplies each genuinely possessed capability at its real owner — GIF frame timing and loop policy, and modern-codec-bridge frame timing and decode working-set estimation — so consumers can retrieve those real values from a location-specific capability accessor rather than from required members on every backend.
rubrics.rationale: Names the hidden capability owners so grading can distinguish a real segregation from capability support being dropped outright; the SWE-Atlas pattern requires verifying the smell relation's legitimate uses survive the refactor.

rubrics.criterion: The capability questions still funnel through one shared surface that every backend must answer (e.g. the required members merely renamed, relocated, or re-expressed as inherited not-applicable trait defaults that every implementor implicitly carries).
rubrics.rationale: Instance-specific failure mode: a mechanical rename or defaults-for-stubs move preserves the fat-interface relation while appearing to refactor; the diff must genuinely segregate, not relabel.

rubrics.criterion: Both generic consumer sites — the animated-output frame-info/loop-count path and the `/v1/estimate` endpoint's decode-side estimate lookup — are updated to obtain the capability through the post-refactor arrangement, leaving no dead calls, unused imports, or unused fields left over from the removed capability surface.
rubrics.rationale: The probes exist because of these two consumers; leaving one wired to removed or dangling surface is the coupled edit this instance cannot skip.

rubrics.criterion: Bridge plumbing that existed only to serve the removed probe path — the decode thread-budget value cached at construction of the modern-codecs bridge so the reported resource estimate could match prior in-situ computation — is removed unless the reworked capability surface genuinely still uses it for the same estimation.
rubrics.rationale: This instance added a dedicated support field/constructor line purely to feed one probe; forgetting it leaves dead state that no longer has a caller, but an alternative repair that legitimately reuses it must not be penalized.

rubrics.criterion: Any change to the JSON estimate endpoint's source is accompanied by a regenerated OpenAPI schema fingerprint record, so the in-tree schema-consistency check passes exactly as before.
rubrics.rationale: Instance-specific trap: the endpoint sources participate in a recorded fingerprint that a test verifies; a behavior-preserving repair that edits this source still fails the suite unless the companion record is refreshed.

rubrics.criterion: Inert per-backend capability stubs, their per-format reason comments, and other dead remnants of the pre-refactor capability surface still exist somewhere in the codecs layer.
rubrics.rationale: The injected stubs and their not-applicable comments are obsolete once the surface is segregated; leaving them behind (including in dead code paths) means the cleanup is incomplete.

rubrics.criterion: Animated-output values are preserved exactly: default frame pacing when no decoder reports timing, the identical delay and loop-count values that GIF and modern-codec inputs produce today, and loop count 0 when nothing reports.
rubrics.rationale: The rewired consumers define the behavior contract for this instance; any parsing-plumbing refactor that shifts these values by even a unit fails the stability requirement the task states.

rubrics.criterion: The decode-side estimates reported through the `/v1/estimate` endpoint are unchanged on capable-decoder paths — same values, same thread-budget-derived inputs — and every other decoder still contributes no estimate.
rubrics.rationale: The estimate endpoint is the one consumer that must not lose its working numbers; silently degrading to no-estimate or skewing the budget inputs is an instance-specific behavioral regression.

rubrics.criterion: Instead of reporting genuine capability or a genuine unknown, the repair makes a capability-less backend fabricate data — invented frame delays, loop counts, or byte estimates that change consumer output.
rubrics.rationale: Plausible shortcut specific to this smell: making every backend answer something real-looking removes the conspicuous stubs while corrupting reporting; the outcome must remain genuine capability or genuine unknown.
